report.summary: Chunk 1 of graph.py: defines identifiers(), name_index(), SymbolResolver, build_resolver(), _dedup(); docstring describes call-graph approach, Move 4 import-aware resolution, backward compatibility, and determinism fix.
risks: SymbolResolver.resolve | medium | The method returns the first import that defines the name; if multiple imports define the same name, order depends on sorted tuple order (deterministic) but may not match programmer intent. This is a design trade-off documented in __post_init__.

build_resolver | low | Uses setdefault and first-definition-wins; if the same unit name appears in multiple units within the same file, only the first is kept. This is documented but may surprise users expecting merge behavior.
name_index | low | Returns list of CodeUnits per name; if multiple units share a name across files, all are returned. This is the old behavior used as fallback.
_dedup | low | Function defined but not used in this chunk; it may be dead code or used later. Its dedup key includes line number, so same unit at different lines is not deduplicated.

handoff.purpose: Define core functions and SymbolResolver for name-based reference graph with import-aware resolution.

symbols.name: identifiers
symbols.note: Returns set of identifier tokens from source, excluding stop-words and tokens <= 2 characters.

symbols.name: name_index
symbols.note: Builds a dict mapping unit name to list of CodeUnits with that name.

symbols.name: SymbolResolver
symbols.note: Dataclass with defs_by_file and imports_by_file; __post_init__ sorts imports for determinism; resolve() performs same-file then import lookup; imports() checks if target_file is imported.

symbols.name: SymbolResolver.defs_by_file
symbols.note: Field: dict mapping file relative path to dict of name->CodeUnit defined in that file.

symbols.name: SymbolResolver.imports_by_file
symbols.note: Field: dict mapping file relative path to sorted tuple of imported file paths.

symbols.name: SymbolResolver.__post_init__
symbols.note: Normalizes imports_by_file values to sorted tuples for deterministic iteration order.

symbols.name: SymbolResolver.resolve
symbols.note: Resolves a name from a file: checks local defs, then defs in imported files in order, returns None if not found.

symbols.name: SymbolResolver.imports
symbols.note: Returns True if target_file is in the imports of from_file.

symbols.name: build_resolver
symbols.note: Builds SymbolResolver from list of CodeUnits and imports_by_file dict; first definition wins per file.

symbols.name: _dedup
symbols.note: Deduplicates CodeUnits by (module, name, line) tuple; defined but not used in this chunk.

symbols.name: _STOP
symbols.note: Set of stop-words (Python keywords plus common cross-language noise words).

claims.text: Compiler-precise, cross-file symbol resolution is SCIP / tree-sitter-stack-graphs territory: months of per-language work. This is the honest v1 — a NAME-based reference graph over the units the parser already extracted: for a unit, which *other known unit names* appear as identifier tokens in its body.
claims.why: The claim about SCIP/stack-graphs and months of work is context not verifiable from this chunk. The description of v1 behavior is consistent with the code: identifiers() extracts identifier tokens, and name_index() maps names to units.

claims.text:
Movement I.5 / Move 4 sharpens it with import/scope awareness. A raw name match picks up EVERY unit that happens to share a name (a ``run`` in ten unrelated files). Given a ``SymbolResolver`` (a per-file symbol table + the Move-2 import edges), resolution instead prefers, in order:
  1. a unit defined in the SAME file as the reference,
  2. a unit in a module the file actually IMPORTS,
  3. the global-name fallback (the old behavior) only when 1+2 find nothing.
claims.why: SymbolResolver.resolve() implements exactly this order: checks local defs, then defs in imported files, returns None (caller does global fallback). The docstring says 'caller does global fallback' and the method returns None in that case.

claims.text: This drops false call edges -> tighter distill slices + a truer call graph.
claims.why: Effect on call graph and slices is not observable from this chunk; requires integration with slice.py.

claims.text: Python is precise (its import graph is precise); other languages are best-effort (their import resolution is best-effort).
claims.why: No code in this chunk handles language-specific import precision; this is a design note.

claims.text: Full scope/shadowing is deliberately NOT attempted here — that is SCIP / stack-graphs, deferred, not faked.
claims.why: No code in this chunk handles scope/shadowing; consistent with the simple name-based approach.

claims.text: Backward-compatible: ``callees``/``callers`` take an OPTIONAL ``resolver`` that defaults to None (the pure name-match), so existing callers (``slice.py``) are unaffected.
claims.why: callees/callers functions are not defined in this chunk; cannot verify backward compatibility.

claims.text: Identifier tokens in a chunk of source, minus obvious stop-words.
claims.why: Function returns set of tokens matching _IDENT regex, filtered by exclusion from _STOP set and length > 2. This matches the docstring description.

claims.text: ``defs_by_file`` — file rel -> {unit name: unit} (the names that file defines; first definition wins on a same-file name collision).
claims.why: In __init__, defs_by_file stores mapping; build_resolver uses setdefault to keep first definition. Verified.

claims.text: ``imports_by_file`` — file rel -> set of internal files it imports (Python precise via ``python_imports``; other languages best-effort via Move 2).
claims.why: The type in the code is dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] (not set), and the source of imports (python_imports, Move 2) is not in this chunk. The docstring says 'set' but code uses tuple (sorted).

claims.text: SORTED TUPLES, not sets. ``resolve`` returns the FIRST import that defines a name, so when two imported modules both define it, WHICH unit is returned is decided by iteration order -- and over a set of rel-path strings that order is a function of PYTHONHASHSEED. The chosen unit reaches the CALLEES block of ``slice_text``, so the distilled slice was not byte-identical across processes (measured: 3 distinct slice hashes over 5 seeds on a 6-module fixture). Normalising HERE rather than in ``build_resolver`` means every construction path is deterministic, including hand-built resolvers. Same candidates, now a total order; ties break on rel path.
claims.why: __post_init__ sorts each value in imports_by_file into a tuple. The docstring explains the determinism issue and the fix. The code matches the description.

claims.text: Best unit for ``name`` referenced from ``from_file``: same-file def, else a def in an imported file, else None (caller does global fallback).
claims.why: resolve() checks local defs, then iterates imports, returns None if not found. Matches description.

claims.text: ``build_resolver`` — it is derived (never hand-kept) and cheap.
claims.why: No performance or usage claim can be verified from this chunk alone.

observations.what: Function _dedup is defined but not called in this chunk; may be dead code or used later.

SymbolResolver.imports_by_file is typed as dict[str, tuple[str,...]] but docstring says 'set of internal files'. The actual type after __post_init__ is tuple, which is consistent with the deterministic order requirement.
identifiers() filters tokens with len(t) > 2, which is not mentioned in its docstring ('minus obvious stop-words'). This is an additional filter that may affect behavior.
build_resolver uses setdefault to keep first definition; if the same unit name appears in multiple units in the same file, only the first is kept. This is documented in SymbolResolver docstring.
